f4.quote: During cooling, the high-temperature disordered BCC phase first separates within a miscibility gap into Ni–Al-lean BCC1 and Ni–Al-rich BCC2 by spinodal decomposition.

f5.quote: Below the ordering transition temperature, Ni–Al-rich BCC products order into B2.

f6.quote: a Ni–Al-lean, Co–Cr–Fe-rich BCC matrix containing Ni–Al-rich ordered B2 nanoparticles and larger B2 particles, while the larger B2 particles themselves contain Ni–Al-lean BCC nanoparticles.

f7.quote: the resulting phase boundaries, compositional modulation, and ordered domains impede dislocation motion and increase hardness.

f8.quote: Higher annealing temperature produced a larger BCC fraction and a higher reported density of ordered B2 precipitates.

f9.quote: quenching from progressively higher temperatures should yield a larger BCC fraction, more pronounced spinodal/ordering features and ordered B2 precipitates, and therefore higher hardness.
